theme: copper and moulded tablet image-text pairing and transfer to seals
question: Do texts on copper, bas-relief and incised tablets pair with their images, share vocabulary within an image class, and recur on seals with the matching field animal?
outcome: Repeated texts stay with one image class in all three genres (p = 0.0001). Held-out image prediction succeeds on bas-relief tablets (24.8% against a 21.5% majority) and incised tablets (57.4% against 48.1%) and fails on copper (19.2% against 26.9%). The frozen within-genre conclusion therefore applies to the Harappa tablets only. Copper class-specific sign groups occur on matching-animal seals 3 times against 3.01 expected (p = 0.62); the test had power 0.91 for a fivefold enrichment and 0.22 for a twofold one.
challenge: The first run treated unlabelled copper tablets as a rival class. Two runs used 2,000 permutations where 10,000 were specified, and Haldane odds ratios were misleading.
remedy: Corrections in runs v2 and v3 with amendments. Parpola (1994; 2008) is cited for the copper tie.
retry_when: Seals and sealings from one excavated deposit, or recoded images for the unlabelled copper tablets, permit a within-context comparison.
